newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Argentina's Menem to kick off Asia tour in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem to kick off Asia tour in Vietnam.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem was due to kick off a three-stop Southeast Asia tour in Vietnam late on Sunday, the first known visit to the communist country by a South American head of state.
Menem, flanked by a business delegation, was scheduled to meet Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet on Monday and attend a series of functions aimed at exploring avenues for commercial cooperation.
Diplomats said the two-day trip was aimed at boosting ties between Argentina and a region containing some of the world's fastest growing economies.
After Vietnam, Menem was to fly to Thailand and then on to Singapore -- a trip encompassing a cross section of states belonging to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Argentina and Vietnam have few ties of significance despite diplomatic relations going back more than two decades.
Vietnam's trade with Argentina totals just $10 million a year.

Vietnam's links with Latin America have have been growing in recent years. Hanoi has long-standing ties with fellow communist state Cuba, and President Le Duc Anh -- not expected to meet Menem because of illness -- visited Brazil in 1995. Local newspapers quoted Argentina's top diplomat in Hanoi as saying the trip might pave the way for a visit by the national soccer squad to Vietnam in the near future.
